claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with ductile FCC lamellae.
The untreated as-cast or as-rolled alloy has a coarse lamellar microstructure lacking fine, coherent precipitates.
Annealing at 600–700 °C for 30–60 minutes induces L12-ordered precipitates in the FCC lamellae.
The annealing treatment can produce uniformly distributed, nanoscale precipitates.
The annealing-induced L12 precipitates are coherent with the FCC matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion through Orowan bowing.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates increases strength.
Precipitate coherency preserves strain compatibility and enables effective strain partitioning in the ductile phase.
Strain compatibility and strain partitioning maintain ductility.
The treatment will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated baseline.
The treatment will maintain or modestly improve ductility relative to the untreated baseline.
Enhanced work hardening and more uniform strain distribution account for the maintained or improved ductility.
Annealing outside the proposed time-temperature window may cause precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency.
Higher temperatures or longer annealing durations may cause detrimental phase changes.
Precipitate coarsening, loss of coherency, or detrimental phase changes would compromise the proposed strength-ductility improvement.
Minor variations in local processing conditions could alter the balance between strength and ductility.
